style.base: A symbolist tarot card illustration in the manner of a hand-painted early twentieth century esoteric arcana deck: flat storybook painting with heavy ink outlines, art-nouveau woodcut feeling, and a slim ornate border frame around the scene. Limited palette of dull gold, oxblood red, midnight blue, sage green and bone white on aged parchment. The subject fills most of the card — large, close and theatrical. The background is sparse and quiet, in the spirit of Piranesi's etchings: the ruins of a vast vaulted hall, broken columns, an empty arch, a fallen capital, one lonely staircase, drawn in fine hatched lines and fading into shadow, with at most one small impossible detail — a stair that quietly returns into itself, or an arch that could not stand. Plenty of empty space; the background never competes with the subject. No moon anywhere. Strange, dreamlike and faintly mischievous; bold silhouette, strong contrast, composed so it still reads clearly when shrunk to a thumbnail.
style.noText: Apart from that number there is no other text, no lettering, no roman numerals, no watermark, no signature.
style.withDigits: Apart from that number and the few digits described in the scene there is no other text, no lettering, no watermark, no signature.
style.number: The card's own number {n} is painted large, bold and centered in the banner at the bottom of the card, in the same aged-ink lettering as the rest of the card.
style.figure: People are painted in the sensual, uncanny manner of symbolist painters like Klimt, Moreau and Khnopff: languid poses, heavy-lidded sidelong gazes, bare shoulders and clinging drapery, faintly erotic but never explicit. When the peg is an object, it stays the clear focus — enormous, or held and presented by such a figure.
style.figureSolemn: People are painted with dignity and restraint, in the grave manner of a history painting: fully clothed, composed, no sensuality whatsoever, no bare skin beyond face and hands. When the peg is an object, it stays the clear focus — enormous, or held by such a figure.
